Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer with its own UI under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Users often ask the in-app AI how to use a feature, and the AI had nothing describing JusPrin's own screens, so it described OrcaSlicer's screens, which JusPrin hides. On 2026-11-11 a guide was started that both people and the AI read, with a process to keep it in line with the app.

What exists, all on branch `claude/guide-window` (pushed to origin; it contains `claude/app-guide`; neither is merged into `jusprin-dev`, and no pull request is open). Start from `claude/guide-window`.
- `docs/guide/print-settings.md`: the one page written so far, with five pictures in `docs/guide/pictures/print-settings/`. `docs/guide/README.md` is the index, the rules for a page, and the "Before a release" steps.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds the skill the AI reads (`skills/guide-<page>/SKILL.md`, generated and committed) from each page. `guide.test.ts` beside it fails when a bold label is not in the app's source, when a section has no harness run, when a picture is missing or unused, and when a page has fewer than three questions.
- `tests/shell/guide_checks.json` and `tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py`: for each page, the shell harness runs that walk its screens in the built app, the named checks the page depends on, and the pictures cropped from those runs.
- `tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json` and `run_guide_tests.py`: how-to questions per page, asked of the model, with a judge reading the answers.
- `scripts/check_guide.py [--ask-ai]` runs all of that in one command.
- Help › "JusPrin guide…" opens a window in the app that lists the pages in the order of `docs/guide/README.md`, searches them and shows them with pictures (commit f63b11d4ee). Its design is a proposal Kenneth has not approved yet.

Kenneth's decisions and words: the guide serves both people and the AI; SEO is set aside; "I don't want it to be too complicated and fancy. What I need is that the document can be brought in sync with the code before we make another release." He was unhappy that the first page was first delivered with steps not checked in the running app and without pictures, and that the work looked one-off. For measuring the AI he chose the Claude subscription with Sonnet 5.5 as model and judge; any paid model run needs his approval for that specific batch first.

Measured for the first page: with the guide listed the AI read it and named the right place in 24 of 24 runs on Sonnet 5.5 and 8 of 8 on DeepSeek V4 Flash; without it, 3 of 24. Not yet measured: whether the AI picks the right guide when several are listed.

Kenneth's communication rules are in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and the project's in `AGENTS.md`: full sentences, no invented labels, proposals marked as proposals, decisions asked in full starting with "Decision needed", outcomes reported with what was tested, under about 500 words.

Task:
Write the six guide pages that are still missing in `docs/guide`, each complete by the existing process, so that `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` passes for all seven pages.

The six areas below are a proposed split that Kenneth has seen but not explicitly approved; if the code shows a better boundary, say so and ask. Divide by what a person is trying to do, not by screen.
1. Projects and files: New, Open…, Open recent, dropping a file, Save, autosave, Version history and Restore, Export project 3MF, the Project tab, the project list on Home.
2. Plates and objects: the Plates tab and its row menus (Arrange, Auto-orient, Split, Fix model, number of instances), + Add model, + Add plate, the Move, Rotate and Scale strip, and More for cut, text and painting.
3. Printers and filament: the printer and filament chip in the header and its menus, plate type, filament colour, adding another filament, adding, connecting, renaming and removing a printer on Home, importing printers, Calibrate….
4. Slicing, checking and printing: the Slice and Print button in each state, Check print, the print issues pill with Ask AI and Ignore this warning, Export sliced file…, Print history, the print report.
5. AI chats, account and credits: New chat, the chats list, reopening an earlier chat, the model and thinking pickers, attachments, credits, signing in, your own API key, connecting an outside AI tool.
6. The app itself: language, theme, units, mouse controls, showing and hiding panels, classic view, updates, Report a problem….

For each page, follow `docs/guide/README.md` ("Writing a page" and "What the command does") and use `docs/guide/print-settings.md` with its entries in `tests/shell/guide_checks.json` and `tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json` as the worked example:
- Write the steps from the code, never from `agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`, which disagrees with the app in several places. Quote on-screen labels exactly, in bold; the test checks each against the source. Say where menus are on a Mac and on Windows and Linux, since they differ.
- Check every section against the running app before calling it written: give it a harness run in `guide_checks.json`, with the named checks the section depends on. The harness's capture modes are documented at the top of `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` (lines 6 to 354); its `HARNESS SETUP …` lines print the text the app actually shows. If no existing mode walks a screen, add the smallest mode or step that does, in the harness.
- Take the pictures from those runs with `tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py`, look at every picture yourself, and correct the page where a picture shows the text is wrong. That happened on the first page.
- Add at least three questions to `guide_questions.json`, written as a person would ask them, each with what a right answer says.
- Add the page to the list in `docs/guide/README.md`, which also sets its order in the Help window.
- The AI's copy of a page may be at most 16 KiB, and its `ai-description` line at most 300 bytes. Make the seven description lines clearly different from each other, because the AI chooses a page by them.
- Text the AI reads must not name OrcaSlicer and calls the product "the app" (`AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts`).

Things already learned that will save time:
- You need your own Release build of `shell_integration_harness`, `jusprin_web` and `agent_bridge_tests` in your own worktree (about 30 minutes at `-j4`; see `AGENTS.md` for the shared-machine build rules and reuse the dependencies under `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64`). Do not use another session's worktree or build folder.
- Pictures the app draws itself (the AI panel's web view, the plates panel) work unattended. Whole-window pictures taken from the screen came out black when the harness was started from the Claude desktop app, for want of the Screen Recording permission; only Kenneth can grant that. Do not put a black picture in a page; the script refuses them.
- A harness run takes real clicks and fails when another window comes to the front; the script retries once. Run one harness at a time.
- Some harness modes have stale checks unrelated to the guide. Depend on named checks, as the first page's `--setup-differences-capture` entry does, and report stale checks you find instead of chasing all of them.
- After adding a page, regenerate `tests/project_prompt/project_tools.json` with `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[project]'`, because each guide adds a line to the tool list every request carries.
- The printer chat on Home does not receive the list of guides; only the project chat does (`AgentHost.cpp`, where `skill_index` is filled).

Measuring the AI: once several pages exist, run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai -- --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --claude-model claude-sonnet-5-5 --claude-judge-model claude-sonnet-5-5` and report, per page, how many questions were answered right and whether the AI read the right guide. This is the first time it has to choose among several. Ask Kenneth before any paid run on another model.

Not part of this task: changing the Help window's design, the system prompt, or CI; merging or opening a pull request. The project's rule is that the live prompt suite runs before anything that changes what the AI reads is merged; name that as remaining, do not run a paid batch without Kenneth's approval.

Done looks like: seven pages in `docs/guide` listed in its README; each new page has pictures taken from the built app, a harness run for every section, and at least three questions; `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` passes for all pages; the full AgentUI test suite, the type check, `agent_bridge_tests '[project]'` and the prompt suite's unit tests pass; the Help window shows all seven pages in the built app. Commit page by page or in one commit on your own branch. Report to Kenneth what was written, what was tested with the results, which pictures are missing and why, and what is still open.

# Help › JusPrin guide window: findings about the guide's text

Written 2026-11-11 by the session that built the window (branch claude/inspiring-aryabhata-8ac5c2). These are about docs/guide/print-settings.md, not the window. Not fixed: that page belongs to the guide work.

Two cold readers (one on the design boards, one on screenshots of the built app) read the page. What they tripped on:

- "Choose **Plate settings…**." ends in "…." because the menu name carries the ellipsis. Same with "Version history…." elsewhere.
- "In the **Plates** tab at the left": the picture next to it shows the Plates tab, but in the app the left pane starts collapsed and shows only a strip reading "Objects · 1", so a reader looking for a "Plates tab" does not find it.
- The plate picture shows Plate 2 with no menu open, so it does not show the step it sits under ("open the plate's "···" menu").
- "The window holds what can differ per plate" names no window; the reader did not know which window opened.
- Jargon a newcomer did not know: presets, print sequence, spiral vase, "once AI is set up".
- In the dark window the pictures stay light (they are light-mode captures). Readable, but they look pasted in. Dark captures would need run_guide_checks.py to take each picture twice.
----
Finish fixing the shell harness's `--printer-setup` run in the JusPrin repo (/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin), so it ends with `HARNESS RESULT PASS failures=0` and the default harness run stays at 0 failures. Then commit.

Where the work is
- Local branch `claude/printer-setup-harness-fixes` (not pushed). Its top commit `a47db8f680` is a WIP commit with the fixes so far. It sits on `claude/guide-window` (pushed; the Help › JusPrin guide window), which sits on `claude/app-guide`. Neither is on `jusprin-dev` yet.
- Make your own worktree from that branch under `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/` and build it there (Release, `-j4`, `shell_integration_harness` target). Don't use another session's worktree.

What was wrong, and what the WIP commit already fixes (each one reproduced before the fix)
- Crash in `MachineObject::reset` and five Bambu connection failures in `verify_saved_bambu_connection`. Since OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 (upstream commits 159e577543c and 5028a5000e6), the device manager's nearby-printer list also holds the LAN printers of other printer agents, here the stand-in Moonraker printers (`127.0.0.1:<port>`) that earlier checks connected. The harness took `candidates.front()` as the fake Bambu printer and got a Moonraker one, so connect was refused as "other_model" and `get_my_machine(device)->reset()` dereferenced null. Fix: the new helper `lists_fake_bambu()` finds the fake by `JUSPRIN_FAKE_BAMBU_DEV_ID`, in all three fixtures that connect it.
- The nozzle-change check found no project versions: an empty project that was never saved stays in memory and keeps none (Kenneth's save rule, 74a0e9b61c). Fix: the check loads a cube first, then goes back to Home.
- The Home card check compared message text that b0a2fe3b08 replaced with the `no_connection` flag. Fix: it reads the flag.
- Closing the Add a printer chat let a waiting connection test save the printer's late answer. Fix: `PrinterConversation::close()`, called from `PrinterPanel::close()`.

What still fails: `selection_interruption_does_not_blame_credentials`
- The check connects the fake Bambu printer, calls `wxYield()` once, deselects it, and expects `connection(name)` to read state "failed" with "The selected printer changed". It reads "connecting".
- What happens during that `wxYield()`, from the app log and lldb: upstream's Device tab handles a backlog of queued `wxEVT_COMMAND_CHOICE_SELECTED` events (`MonitorPanel::on_select_printer`). There are three each for `127.0.0.1:2` and the other stand-in's port, then three more for `127.0.0.1:2`; all are refused as "not in the current agent's machine list". Then one for `FAKE001`, which takes upstream's "same LAN machine: disconnect and reconnect" path. The fake answers the disconnect with ConnectStatusLost, and upstream's local-connect handler (GUI_App.cpp, about line 2470) clears the selection. The backend then sees a Lost answer newer than the connect, reports it before looking at the selection (OrcaPrinterBackend::connection, about line 678), and holds "connecting" while its port look runs.
- Who queues them: upstream `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent()` → `GUI_App::select_machine()` → `MonitorPanel::select_machine()`, which only queues the event. It runs each time a printer preset loads during the earlier `verify_named_printers` checks (for example from `Printers::rename_named_printer` → `Tab::load_config`).
- Open question to settle first: why aren't those queued events handled when they are queued? The harness waits with a one-shot wxTimer, so the event loop should run between checks. Find out whether a real person can hit the same thing (selections piling up behind a hidden Device tab, then clearing a Bambu connection), or whether only the harness's way of driving the app causes it. That decides whether the fix belongs in the harness or in the app. If the fix touches an OrcaSlicer-owned file, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` first.

How to run, and the traps already hit
- `cd build/arm64; HOME=<your scratch>/hhome ./tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --printer-setup > <log> 2>&1`. A run takes 5–25 minutes, longer when the machine is loaded, so run it in the background.
- Run one harness at a time, and never delete the HOME folder of a run that is still going. Two runs at once, sharing one HOME, gave extra timing failures (the host-timeout checks and `home_bambu_error_pause_needs_attention`) that are not real. Check `pgrep -fl JusPrinShellHarness` before every start.
- Check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` before building. Load from other sessions reached 24 on 12 cores and makes the host-timeout checks flaky.
- The app log is in the run's data dir (`HARNESS DATA DIR kept for inspection: …` at the end of the output), under `log/`. Delete only the data dirs your own runs print.
- In this Release build lldb can't read arguments by name. For `set_selected_machine(std::string)` use `memory read -f s -c 1 '$x1+1'` (a short string's text starts one byte in) and `bt`.
- After restoring a file from a copy, `touch` it, or ninja won't recompile it.

Done when
- `--printer-setup` passes with 0 failures, twice in a row, each run on its own.
- The default harness run (no flag) passes with 0 failures.
- The fix for the last check is reproduced failing before and passing after.
- The include check passes on the changed lines: `scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh`.
- The WIP commit is replaced by a finished commit (or commits) on `claude/printer-setup-harness-fixes`, with a message that says what was wrong, how it was fixed, and what was tested.
- Don't push or open a PR unless Kenneth asks. Report to Kenneth in his style: under 500 words, outcomes not the journey, and any decision asked in full starting with "Decision needed".

# JusPrin guide

How to use JusPrin, one page per part of the app. The same pages are in the app, under Help › JusPrin guide…, in the order of the list below.

- [Seeing and changing print settings](print-settings.md)

## Before a release

The guide is brought in line with the app before each release, on a computer with the app built.

1. Build the app's test harness and pages from the commit to release: the `shell_integration_harness` and `jusprin_web` targets.
2. Leave the computer alone and run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. It takes about a minute a page, plus the questions.
3. Fix what it reports, then run it again until it passes:
   - **A label is on no screen.** The app's wording changed. Find the new wording in the app and correct the page.
   - **A run failed.** Open its log, which the command names. Either the screen no longer works as the page says, and the page needs correcting, or the harness expects something the app no longer does, and the harness needs correcting.
   - **A picture is blank.** The program that started the command may not record the screen. Grant it Screen Recording in the system's privacy settings and run again.
   - **AI answered a question wrongly.** Read its reply in the output. Usually the page is unclear or its first line does not say when to read it.
4. Look through what changed on screen since the last release (`git log <last release tag>..HEAD -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin`). The command finds what a page gets wrong. It cannot find a new screen or menu item that no page mentions, so add those by hand.
5. Commit the pages together with their pictures and the skills the command rebuilt.

## What the command does

1. **Walks the app and takes the pictures.** `tests/shell/guide_checks.json` names, for each page, the runs of the app's test harness that go through the screens the page describes, and the checks in each run the page depends on. `tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py` runs them in the app as built and copies the pictures a page uses into `pictures/<page>/`.
2. **Rebuilds the copy AI reads.** `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds a skill from each page.
3. **Checks each page**, in `guide.test.ts` beside it: every label in bold is in the app's source, every section has a run in step 1, every picture is one step 1 took, and the page has questions for step 4. `components/Guide.test.tsx` checks that the app's guide window lists every page and shows each with all its pictures and without the parts written for AI.
4. **Asks AI the page's questions** (`--ask-ai`). `tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json` holds them with what a right answer says. `tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py` asks the model and has a judge read the replies.

## Writing a page

- Start it with `<!-- ai-description: … -->`: one line, at most 300 bytes, saying when AI should read it.
- Put words that are only for AI in `<!-- ai: … -->`. They are hidden on this site.
- Use bold only for words that are on screen, exactly as they are on screen.
- A picture goes on a line of its own, as `![what it shows](pictures/<page>/<name>.png)`, and comes from a run named in `guide_checks.json`. AI's copy leaves it out.
- A picture is kept at twice the screen's size, and the guide window shows it at half, the size it has on screen. Mark a run's picture that the harness draws at the screen's own size with `"atScreenSize": true`, and the command doubles it.
- List a new page at the top of this file, or the guide window leaves it out.
- Give each `##` section a run in `guide_checks.json`.
- Add at least three questions for the page to `guide_questions.json`.
- AI's copy may hold at most 16 KiB. Split a page that grows past that.

# Seeing and changing print settings

Where the settings of a print are shown in JusPrin, and the ways to change them.

Names in bold are the words on screen. On a Mac the menus named here are in the menu bar. On Windows and Linux they are inside the menu at the left of the title bar.

<!-- ai: This guide is the by-hand route. When the person wants a setting changed and has not said they want to do it themselves, I change it with my settings tools. I give these steps when they ask where something is or want to do it themselves. -->

## See the settings a print will use

The **Setup summary** card at the top of the AI panel names the process and filament presets in use and says how many settings differ from them. If the AI panel is hidden, open the **View** menu and choose **Show AI panel** (on Windows and Linux, tick **AI panel**).

![The Setup summary card at the top of the AI panel, with the All settings link at its right](pictures/print-settings/setup-summary.png)

To see every setting:

1. On the Setup summary card, click **All settings**. The link is there once AI is set up.
2. Under **Showing**, pick **Whole project**, one plate, or one object. Plates are listed when the project has two or more. The list also follows what is selected in the 3D view.
3. Type in **Search settings** to find a setting by name, or switch from **All** to **Changed** to see only the settings that differ from the presets.
4. Click **Back to chat** to close the list.

![The All settings list, showing the whole project, with the Search settings box and the All and Changed switch](pictures/print-settings/all-settings.png)

The settings are grouped as Quality, Strength, Speed, Support, Multimaterial and Others, then Filament and Printer. The list is for reading: a value cannot be typed into it.

## Change a print setting

Print settings are things like layer height, infill, supports and speed. JusPrin's own view has no field to type them into. There are two ways to change one:

- Ask AI in the chat, for example "set the layer height to 0.16 mm". The change is then listed in the chat with the old and the new value.
- Switch to classic view, which has every print setting on screen. See [Classic view](#classic-view-every-setting-on-screen).

## Take a settings change back

- Each change made in a chat is listed in that chat. Point at a change and click the curved-arrow button at its right, named **Revert to here**. Then click **Revert to here** in the question that opens. The model and the project's settings go back to that point. The current model is saved in Version history first, and the chat, exported files and finished prints stay as they are.

![The Revert to here question over a list of changes in a chat](pictures/print-settings/revert-to-here.png)
- When a preset was saved from the chat, a line reading "Saved:" with the preset's name follows. Click **Undo** on that line to bring its earlier values back.
- To go back to an earlier state of the whole project, open the **File** menu and choose **Version history…**.

## Change printer or filament settings

These open a window with every setting of the printer or of a filament.

- Printer: click the printer's name in the header of the project, then **Printer settings…**. The **Printer** menu has the same item. With no printer chosen yet, it starts adding a printer.
- Filament: click the filament in the header of the project, then **Filament settings…**. With several filaments, pick one from the list first. The **Printer** menu has the same item for the first filament.

## Settings for one plate

1. In the **Plates** tab at the left, open the plate's "⋯" menu, or right-click the plate.
2. Choose **Plate settings…**.

![The Plates tab, with the ⋯ button at the right of a plate's row](pictures/print-settings/plates-tab.png)

The window holds what can differ per plate: the plate's name, its bed type, the print sequence, spiral vase, and the filament sequence of the first and the other layers. A setting made there shows in All settings with the note "Set on this plate".

## Settings for one object

An object can have settings of its own that differ from the project's. Its row in the **Plates** tab then carries a diamond mark, and the mark's menu says how many it has.

- To see them, open **All settings** and pick the object under **Showing**.
- To take one off, click **Use project value** on its row. A support blocker or enforcer has **Remove**.
- To add one or edit its value, ask AI in the chat, or use classic view.

![All settings showing one object, with Use project value beside its own Wall loops and Remove beside a support blocker](pictures/print-settings/object-settings.png)

## Classic view: every setting on screen

Classic view is the app's original screen, with all print settings in a panel at the side.

1. Open the **View** menu and choose **Switch to classic view…**. The "…" button in the header of the project has the same item.
2. A bar across the top says the window is in classic view. Click **Back to JusPrin** on it to return. The **View** menu also has **Switch to JusPrin view**.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Does the project chat's model answer a how-to question from the app guide?

Each question in guide_questions.json belongs to one page of docs/guide. A run
sends the question as a chat's first message and passes when the model's reply
tells the person what the question's "answer" says, in the judge's reading. The
run's line also says whether the model read the page's skill
(skills/guide-<area>/SKILL.md) on the way.

The request is the recorded "advice-infill" point with the person's sentence
replaced, so the prompt, the tools and the workspace are the app's, and a
skill_read of a guide is answered with the skill as checked in. Everything
else is run_prompt_tests.py: the same options, backends and judge.

    tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --runs 1
    tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py --area print-settings --no-guide ...

--area keeps the questions of one page. --no-guide takes every guide off the
list skill_read carries, which is the app before the guide: the gap between
the two runs is what the guide does.
"""
import copy
import json
import pathlib
import sys

import run_prompt_tests as runner

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SKILLS = HERE / "../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills"
QUESTIONS = json.loads((HERE / "guide_questions.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
POINT = "advice-infill"


def skill_text(area):
    """The text skill_read returns: the skill file after its front matter."""
    return (SKILLS / f"guide-{area}" / "SKILL.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8").split("\n---\n", 1)[1].strip()


def add_case(area, entry, with_guide):
    skill = f"guide-{area}"

    class GuideQuestion(runner.Case):
        def check(self, step):
            if step.tool:
                return (runner.FAIL if step.changes() else runner.CONTINUE), str(step)
            read = any("skill_read" in line and skill in line for line in self.log)
            yes, why = self.judged(step, f"Does the assistant's last message tell the person {entry['answer']}?")
            tag = "[read the guide] " if read else "[did not read the guide] "
            return (runner.PASS, tag + str(step)) if yes else (runner.FAIL, tag + "WRONG OR MISSING PLACE: " + why)

    GuideQuestion.name = f"guide-{area}-{entry['id']}"
    GuideQuestion.__doc__ = entry["question"]
    point = copy.deepcopy(runner.REQUESTS[POINT])
    point["body"]["input"][0]["content"][0]["text"] = entry["question"]
    if with_guide:
        answer = copy.deepcopy(next(a for a in point["answers"] if a["tool"] == "skill_read"))
        output = json.loads(answer["output"])
        output["result"] = {"name": skill, "text": skill_text(area)}
        answer["arguments"] = {"name": skill}
        answer["output"] = json.dumps(output, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
        point["answers"].append(answer)
    runner.REQUESTS[GuideQuestion.name] = point
    runner.CASES[GuideQuestion.name] = GuideQuestion
    return GuideQuestion.name


def take(flag, has_value):
    """Removes this script's own option from the command line and returns it."""
    if flag not in sys.argv:
        return None
    at = sys.argv.index(flag)
    value = sys.argv[at + 1] if has_value else True
    del sys.argv[at:at + (2 if has_value else 1)]
    return value


def main():
    area = take("--area", True)
    with_guide = not take("--no-guide", False)

## 2. How it behaves

- **Where projects are stored:** `<data_dir>/jusprin/projects/<project-id>/` (`ShellController.cpp:438-442`).
- **When autosave saves.** A timer runs every 33 ms (`:715`). Autosave checks for changes every 2 s. It saves the model 1.5 s after the last edit, but not while a tool edit is in progress or an AI turn is running. Chat-only changes are written within 15 s at most (`Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:39-41, 632-684`).
- **Blank projects are never saved.** A project is saved once it holds a model, and stays saved after that (`ProjectAutosave.hpp:112-114`). An unnamed project takes its first object's file name (`ProjectAutosave.cpp:547-552`).
- **How many versions are kept:** up to 200 versions or 4 GB. Pinned versions are kept regardless: Save, Restore and AI before/after versions (`ProjectAutosave.cpp:42-43`, `Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:943-992`).
- **What Restore does.** It saves the current state first, pins both versions, reloads the chosen model and settings, keeps the chats, and brings marked regions back with the model. It adds an undo boundary named "Restore project version" (`ProjectAutosave.cpp:1087-1152`).
- **Export** saves first, then writes through a temporary file (`:1215-1235`). It leaves out the chat state (inferred from harness check `exported_archive_excludes_managed_state`, which tested OrcaSlicer's export path).
- **Files opened from Finder/Explorer, Open… or a drop on Home** open as a new project (`ShellController.cpp:1019-1072`).
  - A Home drop is first copied to `<temp>/JusPrin-dropped/<md5>/` and is left out of recent files (`OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1395-1437`).
  - If that copy fails: "%s couldn't be opened. Try opening it with Open… instead."
- **A model dropped on the canvas** is added to the open project (`ShellController.cpp:262-290, 1074-1080`).
- **A .3mf opened anywhere** (including a drop on the canvas) opens as a project. If it was opened before, a "Previously opened file" dialog asks. Its buttons are "Continue current project", "Open existing project" or "Open most recent project", and "Create new project". If the file has changed since, "Create new project" becomes the default (`ShellController.cpp:575-650`).

<!-- ai-description: Read before telling the person how to start, open, save, find or export a project by hand: New, Open…, Open recent, dropping a file, autosave and Save, Version history and Restore, Export project 3MF, the Project tab, and the project list on Home. -->

# Projects and files

How JusPrin keeps your work, and how to open, save and export it.

Names in bold are the words on screen. On a Mac the menus named here are in the menu bar. On Windows and Linux the **File** menu is the **File** button in the title bar, and the other menus are in the menu beside it.

<!-- ai: These are the by-hand steps. I can open a file the person attached for them; I cannot save, restore or export a project myself, so for those I give these steps. -->

## Start a project or open a file

Every project is kept by JusPrin itself, in its own folder of projects. A file you open is copied into a new project; the file itself is left as it was.

- **New project** in the **File** menu, or **New** on Home, starts an empty project. The project you were in is saved first.
- **Open…** in the **File** menu, or **Open…** on Home, opens a model or a project file as a new project. The files it opens are STL, 3MF, STEP, OBJ, AMF, SVG and ZIP.
- Dropping a file on Home, or opening one from Finder or Explorer, also opens it as a new project.
- Dropping a model on the 3D view of an open project adds it to that project. A 3MF file opens as a project of its own wherever it is dropped.
- **Open recent** in the **File** menu lists the last ten projects, newest first. It is greyed out while there are none.

The shortcuts are Cmd+N and Cmd+O on a Mac, Ctrl+N and Ctrl+O on Windows and Linux.

## Open a file you opened before

When you open a 3MF file that is already one of your projects, JusPrin asks what to do before it opens anything:

- **Continue current project** keeps working in the project that is open.
- **Open existing project** (or **Open most recent project**, when the file made more than one) goes to the project you made from it before.
- **Create new project** opens the file again as a separate project. When the file has changed since you last opened it, this is the button already chosen.

![The question asked when a 3MF file that is already a project is opened again](pictures/projects-and-files/reopen-question.png)

## Saving

JusPrin saves the project by itself: a moment after you stop changing it, and never while AI is in the middle of a change. The project's name in the header of the project is followed by **Saving…**, **Saved** or **Couldn't save**.

- **Save** in the **File** menu (Cmd+S on a Mac, Ctrl+S on Windows and Linux) saves now and keeps that version for good, so it stays in Version history.
- An empty project is never saved. It is saved once it holds a model, and from then on even if you empty it.
- A project without a name takes the name of the first model in it.
- If saving fails, for example because the disk is full, the "…" menu at the right of the header says **Changes couldn't be saved. JusPrin will retry.**, and saving starts again by itself once it can.

## Go back to an earlier version

Each save is kept as a version. JusPrin keeps up to 200 of them, and always keeps the ones you saved with Save and the ones from before and after a change AI made.

1. Choose **Version history…** in the **File** menu, or **Version history** in the "…" menu at the right of the header. The panel at the left opens on the project's versions, newest first.
2. Click **Restore** beside the version you want. Clicking the time does nothing.
3. Click **Restore** in the question that opens.

![The project's versions in the panel at the left, each with a Restore button](pictures/projects-and-files/version-history.png)

The model and the project's settings go back to that version. What you had is saved as a version first, so you can go back to it the same way. Chats and print records stay as they are.

To take back one change AI made in a chat, use **Revert to here** beside the change instead; the guide's page on print settings describes it.

## Export the project as a 3MF file

Projects stay in JusPrin's own folder. To give a project to someone, or to open it in another program, export it:

1. Choose **Export project 3MF…** in the "…" menu at the right of the header, or in the File menu choose **Export**, then **Project 3MF…** (Cmd+Shift+S on a Mac, Ctrl+Shift+S on Windows and Linux).
2. Pick where to save it. It is saved first, then written there.

The 3MF file holds the model, the plates and the settings. It does not hold the chats.

## The Project tab

The panel at the left of the 3D view has two tabs, **Plates** and **Project**. It starts hidden: click the button at the left of the header, or choose **Plates and project panel** in the **View** menu, to show it. Then click **Project**.

![The Project tab, with the project's name, its model information and the Print history, Details, Version history and Export project 3MF… rows](pictures/projects-and-files/project-tab.png)

- The top shows the project's name and whether it is saved.
- **MODEL** shows the model's title, designer and picture, when the file brought them. Otherwise it says **No title, designer or description yet.** with **+ Edit Project Info** to add them.
- **Print history**, **Details**, **Version history** and **Export project 3MF…** open those. Details holds the description, the attached files and the designer's profile.

## Your projects on Home

Home lists every project under **Projects**, most recent first, each with a picture of its plate, its name, when it was saved and what happened to it last, such as printed or exported. Click a project to open it.

To get to Home from a project, click the house button at the left of the header, or choose **Home** in the **View** menu.

![Home, with a project in the Projects list beside the tile for dropping a file](pictures/projects-and-files/home-projects.png)

- With eight projects or more, **Search projects** and a choice between **Recent** and **Name** appear above the list.
- Dropping a file anywhere on Home opens it as a new project.
- A project cannot be renamed or deleted from Home.

<!-- ai-description: Read before telling the person how to arrange things by hand on the plates: the Plates tab and its plate and object menus (Arrange, Auto-orient, Split, Fix model, number of instances), Add model, Add plate, the Move, Rotate and Scale tools on the 3D view, More, and cut or paint keys. -->

# Plates and objects

How to put models on plates and move, turn, size, copy and split them by hand.

Names in bold are the words on screen. On a Mac the menus named here are in the menu bar. On Windows and Linux they are in the menu beside the **File** button in the title bar.

<!-- ai: These are the by-hand steps. I can import, place, lay out, repair and split objects myself with my tools when the person asks me to; I give these steps when they want to do it themselves or ask where something is. -->

## The Plates tab

The panel at the left of the 3D view lists the project's plates and what is on each. It starts hidden. To show it, click the button at the far left of the header (**Show the Plates and Project panel**), or choose **Show plates and project panel** in the **View** menu (on Windows and Linux, tick **Plates and project panel**). The panel has two tabs; **Plates** is the first.

![The Plates tab with two plates, the first open with its object, and the Add model and Add plate buttons under the list](pictures/plates-and-objects/plates-tab.png)

- Each plate's row says whether it is sliced: **Sliced**, **Not sliced yet** or **Slicing…**.
- Click a plate to make it the plate you are working on. Only that plate is open in the list; a closed plate shows a short summary such as its object's name or how many objects it holds.
- Click an object to select it in the 3D view. Selecting an object in the 3D view selects it here too.
- A row may carry **Mesh needs repair**, **won't print**, the number of its filament, or "×2" and more for copies.
- A diamond mark on a row means the plate or object has settings or painting of its own. Click it to see which.

## A plate's menu

Point at a plate's row and click the "⋯" button at its right, or right-click the row. The menu has:

- **Rename** to name the plate.
- **Arrange** to lay out the objects on this plate only.
- **Auto-orient** to turn this plate's objects to the side that prints best.
- **Lock** to keep Arrange from moving this plate's objects. **Unlock** undoes it.
- **Plate settings…** for what can differ per plate, such as its bed type. The guide's page on print settings describes the window.
- **Move to front**, on plates after the first, to make it plate 1.
- **Delete plate**, when the plate can be deleted.

## An object's menu

Point at an object's row and click "⋯", or right-click the row:

- **Rename** to name the object.
- **Set number of instances…** to print several copies of it. Each copy then has a row of its own, with **Delete copy** in its menu.
- **Printable** to leave the object on the plate without printing it. Its row then says **won't print**.
- **Change filament**, when the print uses more than one filament, to print the object in another one.
- **Fix model**, when the model's mesh has errors, to repair it.
- **Split**, then **To objects** to make each separate piece its own object, or **To parts** to keep the pieces as parts of one object.
- **Delete** to take the object off the plate.

![An object's menu in the Plates tab, with Rename, Set number of instances…, Printable, Split and Delete](pictures/plates-and-objects/object-menu.png)

## Add a model or a plate

Under the list in the Plates tab:

- **Add model** opens a file and adds it to the plate you are working on. Dropping a model on the 3D view does the same.
- **Add plate** adds an empty plate after the last one. It is greyed out when no more plates fit.

With nothing in the project, the 3D view says **Drop a model here or add one**.

## Move, rotate and scale an object

Select an object, and a row of buttons appears at the top left of the 3D view: Move, Rotate, Scale, a button that adds a copy, and **More**. The keys M, R and S open the first three as well.

![The Rotate tool open under the row of buttons, with the angle typed in](pictures/plates-and-objects/rotate-tool.png)

- **Move**: drag the arrows in the 3D view, or type a position under **Position**. **World coordinates** or **Object coordinates** chooses which way the axes point.
- **Rotate**: type an angle under **Rotate (relative)** to turn the object by it, or under **Rotate (absolute)** to set its angle. Press Return to apply what you typed. A reset button beside a row puts the angle back to where it was when the tool opened.
- **Scale**: type a percentage under **Scale** or a size in mm under **Size**. **Uniform scale** keeps the proportions.
- Click the tool's button again, or **Done**, to close it.
- The copy button (**Add instance**) adds one copy of the selected object. Undo takes it away again.

## More: mirror, text and other tools

**More**, the last button in the row, opens the object menu of the 3D view, the same one a right-click on an object opens. It has **Clone**, **Mirror**, the parts and modifiers you can add, including **Text**, and the object's other commands.

Cutting and painting have no button. With an object selected, press a key in the 3D view:

- C to cut the object in two.
- L to paint where supports go, P to paint where seams go, N to paint colours on a multi-material print, H to paint fuzzy skin.
- F to lay a chosen face flat on the plate.
- T to add text on the object.

Each tool shows its own controls on the 3D view. Press Escape, or the same key, to close it.

<!-- ai-description: Read before telling the person how to choose, add, connect, rename or remove a printer, or choose the plate type, filament, filament colour or a second filament by hand: the printer and filament chip in the project's header, the Printer menu, printer cards on Home, importing printers, and Calibrate…. -->

# Printers and filament

How to choose the printer and filament a project prints with, and how to add and manage your printers.

Names in bold are the words on screen. On a Mac the menus named here are in the menu bar. On Windows and Linux the **File** menu is the **File** button in the title bar, and the other menus are in the menu beside it.

<!-- ai: These are the by-hand steps. I can change printer and filament settings myself with my settings tools; adding and connecting a printer happens in the printer's own chat, which these steps open. -->

## The printer and filament in a project

The header of an open project shows the project's printer and its filament side by side, for example "Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4" and "PLA". With none chosen they read **Select printer** and **Select filament**. Click either one to open its menu.

![The printer and filament in the header of a project](pictures/printers-and-filament/header-chip.png)

The printer's menu has:

- The printer's name and how it is connected, such as **Ready**, **Printing**, **Offline** or **Not connected**. Click it to open the printer's own window.
- **Nozzle**, the nozzle size the project is set up for. It cannot be changed here.
- **Plate**: click it to choose the plate type that is on the printer, such as a textured or a smooth plate.
- **OTHER PRINTERS**: click one to slice the project for that printer instead.
- **Printer settings…**, **Ask AI about printer settings…**, **Calibrate…** and **Add a printer…**.

When a project file brought its own printer, the printer is marked **From the file · not one of your printers**.

## Choose the filament and its colour

Click the filament in the header. The menu has:

- **COLOUR**: click a colour to set the filament's colour. The last one, **Other colour…**, opens a colour picker.
- **FILAMENTS FOR THIS PRINTER**: click one to print with it, or **Other filament…** to pick from all of them.
- **Use what's loaded on the printer…**, when the printer reports what is loaded in it.
- **Filament settings…**, **Ask AI about filament settings…** and **Calibrate this filament…**.

To print in two or more filaments, click **Add another filament to this print**. The menu then lists each filament by its number; click one to choose its filament and colour. To say which filament an object prints in, use **Change filament** in its menu in the Plates tab.

![The filament menu, with the colours, the filaments for this printer, and Add another filament to this print](pictures/printers-and-filament/filament-menu.png)

## The Printer menu

The **Printer** menu has the same commands for the open project: **Add a printer…**, **Printer settings…**, **Ask AI about printer settings…**, **Filament settings…**, **Ask AI about filament settings…** and **Calibrate…**. It works from Home too.

With no printer chosen yet, **Printer settings…** starts adding a printer instead, and **Calibrate…** is greyed out.

## Add a printer

1. On Home, click **+ Add printer** at the top of the printers, or choose **Add a printer…** in the **Printer** menu. A chat titled **Add a printer** opens.
2. Say which printer you have, in your own words, or pick it from a list: **Browse the full printer list** at the top of the chat opens a form that asks **Which printer?** and then **Which plate is on it?**.
3. The printer is saved under its own name and shows on Home. You can add two printers of the same model; each gets a name of its own.

If you skipped choosing a printer the first time JusPrin started, it uses a stand-in, a generic 250 mm Klipper printer, until you add yours.

## Connect a printer

Connecting a printer lets JusPrin send prints to it and show how it is doing. JusPrin connects Bambu Lab printers, and printers that run Klipper with Moonraker or OctoPrint.

1. On Home, click **Connect…** on the printer's card, or open the card's menu (**Printer actions**) and choose **Connect…**.
2. The printer's chat asks for what it needs, such as its address. A Bambu Lab printer also needs its **Access code**, and a print host may need its **API key**. These stay on this computer.
3. **Help me find the code** explains where to find it on the printer.

A Bambu Lab printer needs Bambu's network plug-in. The chat says so when it is missing.

## Rename or remove a printer

Open the printer card's menu on Home (**Printer actions**):

- **Rename**, then type the new name under **Printer name** and click **Save**. A name cannot be empty, hold any of < > [ ] : / \ | ? * ", or be the name of another printer.
- **Remove printer…**, then **Remove**. The printer's own settings are deleted; your projects stay.
- **Printer settings…** and **Ask AI about printer settings…** open its settings.

## Bring printers from another slicer

In the **File** menu choose **Import**, then **Import from OrcaSlicer...** or **Import from JusPrin 1...**. The printers come with their filaments and print settings, and the other program keeps its own copy. JusPrin offers the same the first time it starts, when it finds them on the computer.

## Calibrate a printer or a filament

Calibration prints a small test, such as a temperature tower, and then sets the printer or filament from what the test shows.

1. Choose **Calibrate…** in the printer's menu, the **Printer** menu or the printer card's menu on Home, or **Calibrate this filament…** in the filament's menu.
2. A question names the printer and filament. Click **Start**. The open project is saved and closed, and the test opens as a project of its own, with a chat that asks which test to print.

Calibration needs AI. When it is not set up, the question offers **Set up AI…** instead of Start.

# Slicing, checking and printing

How to turn a project into a print: slice it, check it, and send it to the printer or save the file.

Names in bold are the words on screen. On a Mac the menus named here are in the menu bar. On Windows and Linux they are in the menu beside the **File** button in the title bar.

<!-- ai: These are the by-hand steps. I can slice and check a plate myself with my tools, and open the window that sends a print; the person always sends the print themselves. -->

## Slice and print

The button at the right of the header of the project does the next step for the plate you are working on:

- **Slice** while the plate is not sliced. Cmd+R on a Mac, Ctrl+R on Windows and Linux, does the same.
- **Slicing…** while it slices. The button beside it turns into an X, **Cancel slicing**, that stops it.
- **Print** once the plate is sliced, or **Print plate 2** and so on when the project has more plates. It opens the window that sends the print to the printer, where you start it. Switching to a plate that is not sliced brings **Slice** back.

The arrow beside the button (**Print actions**) has the other choices: **Slice all plates**, and once a plate is sliced, **Check Print**, **Print all plates…** and **Export sliced file…**. The **Print** menu has the same commands.

![The header of a sliced project, with Print plate 2 and the arrow beside it](pictures/slicing-and-printing/print-button.png)

When the printer is not connected, Print says **Printer connection required**: connect the printer first (the guide's page on printers describes it), or save the sliced file and print from a card.

## Check the print before printing

Choose **Check Print** in the menu beside the Print button, or **Check print…** in the **Print** menu. A window opens with the sliced plate and a report beside it.

- The report lists the print's **Time**, **Filament** and **Cost**, then what may need a look: **Supports**, **Seams**, **Slicer warnings**, **First layer**, **Unsupported islands**, **Crossing paths** and **Paths outside the plate**. When there is nothing to look at it says **Nothing to flag.**
- Click a finding to turn the view to it and show its layer.
- **Legend** shows what each colour of the sliced paths means.
- Close the window with the X at its top right or Escape. It also closes by itself when the plate changes and the slice is out of date.

![The Check print report for a plate with nothing to flag](pictures/slicing-and-printing/check-print.png)

## Print issues on the 3D view

When something about the plate would print badly or not at all, a button at the bottom right of the 3D view says how many issues there are, for example "2 print issues". Click it to see them. A bubble then points at the object each issue is about.

![A print issue's bubble beside its object, with Ask AI and Ignore this warning](pictures/slicing-and-printing/print-issue.png)

- **Ask AI** asks AI in the chat to explain the issue and what you can do about it.
- **Ignore this warning** stops counting a warning you have decided to live with. It stays in the list marked **Ignored**; open it there and click **Stop ignoring** to count it again. An issue that keeps the plate from printing cannot be ignored.
- The arrows in the bubble go to the next issue. The X, Escape, or a click on an empty part of the 3D view closes the bubble.

## Save the sliced file instead of sending it

Choose **Export sliced file…** in the menu beside the Print button, or in the **Print** menu, and pick where to save it. Take that file to the printer, for example on a memory card.

## Print history

JusPrin keeps a record of every sliced file it sent or saved, with a copy of the file.

- On Home, click **Print history** above the projects, or the history line on a project's or a printer's card.
- In a project, click **Print history** in the Project tab of the panel at the left.

![Print history, with an exported file and the Print again and Export… buttons](pictures/slicing-and-printing/print-history.png)

Each entry says where the file went and when, and whether the print finished. **Print again** sends the kept copy to the printer again, **Export…** saves it again, and **Open in chat** goes to the chat the print was made in. Type in **Search prints** to find one.

## Tell us how a print came out

When you are signed in to a JusPrin account, an entry in Print history offers **Share how it printed and get 25 credits**. It opens **Tell us how it printed**: add a photo with **Choose a photo…**, write what happened in at least 200 characters, say whether **It worked**, came out **Partly** or not, and click **Send report**. Each sliced file takes one report.

<!-- ai-description: Read before explaining how the AI panel and its chats work or how AI is set up: New chat, the chats list, reopening an earlier chat, the model and thinking pickers, attaching files, credits, signing in to a JusPrin account, using your own API key, and connecting an outside AI tool. -->

# AI chats, account and credits

How to talk with AI about a project, and how to set up the AI it uses.

Names in bold are the words on screen. On a Mac the menus named here are in the menu bar. On Windows and Linux they are in the menu beside the **File** button in the title bar.

<!-- ai: This page is about me and how the person reaches me. When they ask what I can do, I answer from what I can do; these steps are for where things are on screen. -->

## The AI panel and its chats

The AI panel is at the right of an open project. If it is hidden, click the button at the right end of the header (**Show the AI panel**), or choose **Show AI panel** in the **View** menu (on Windows and Linux, tick **AI panel**).

Chats belong to the project they were started in, and are saved with it.

- **New chat**, the + at the top of the panel, starts a chat. It is greyed out while AI is replying.
- **Back to chats**, the arrow at the top left, shows the project's chats, newest first. Click one to open it.
- **Chat actions**, the "⋯" at the top, has **Rename** and **Delete**. Deleting a chat leaves the project and its print history as they are.
- Type in the box at the bottom and press Return to send; Shift+Return starts a new line. While AI replies, the send button becomes **Stop**.
- When AI ends a reply with choices, they show as buttons under it. Click one to answer with it, or type your own answer.

## Open an earlier chat

When the project has not changed since a chat's last turn, the chat simply opens and carries on.

When the project has changed since, the chat opens for reading only, with a note in place of the message box:

- **Restore and resume** puts the project back the way it was in that chat, then lets you carry on there. It asks first; what you have now stays in Version history.
- **Return to active chat** goes back to the chat you were in.
- **Ask current chat about this** quotes the earlier chat in your current one.

![An earlier chat opened for reading, with Restore and resume, Return to active chat and Ask current chat about this](pictures/ai-chats-and-account/earlier-chat.png)

## Choose the model and how hard it thinks

The two choices beside the message box set which AI model the chat uses and how long it thinks before answering. Models from a JusPrin account show how many credits a message costs.

A chat keeps the model and thinking it started with: both are locked once you send the first message. To use another model, start a new chat. To set the model new chats start with, open Preferences, then **BYOAI**, and choose under **New chats start with**.

## Attach a picture or a file

Click **Attach a file**, the + in the message box, and pick **Photo or image**, **3D model (STL, 3MF, STEP)**, **G-code** or **Document (PDF)**. You can also drop files on the message box or paste a picture. Each file shows as a row above the box, with **Remove** to take it off again.

A model that cannot see pictures says so on the picture's row, and the picture is not sent.

## Set up AI

With no AI set up, the panel says **No AI connected** and offers **Set up AI**, which opens Preferences on **Account**. There are three ways, and any of them works on its own:

- A JusPrin account: sign up, and JusPrin's own AI works with credits. See [Sign in](#sign-in-to-a-jusprin-account).
- Your own API key from an AI provider, billed by them. See [Your own API key](#use-your-own-api-key).
- An AI app you already use on this computer, which then works on the open project. See [Connect an AI tool](#connect-an-ai-tool-you-already-use).

To open Preferences: on a Mac choose **Preferences** in the JusPrin menu (Cmd+,); on Windows and Linux choose **Preferences** in the menu beside the **File** button (Ctrl+,). The "…" button at the right of the header also has **Preferences…**.

## Sign in to a JusPrin account

In Preferences, open **Account**.

- **Continue with Google** signs in through your browser. Come back to JusPrin when the browser says you are done.
- Or type your email address and click **Sign up free**, or **Sign in** for an account you have. JusPrin emails you a 6-digit code to type in. **Use a password instead** works for an account that has one.

![Preferences, Account, signed out, with Continue with Google and the email box](pictures/ai-chats-and-account/account.png)

Once signed in, Account shows the email address, the plan and the credits left, with **Get more credits**, **Billing and usage**, **Sign out** and **Delete account…**. Signing out keeps your projects, printers and API keys on this computer.

## Credits

With a JusPrin account, each message costs credits: the cheaper model costs fewer than the stronger one, and the model picker shows how many. A new account starts with free credits, and credits that run out soonest are spent first.

- The ring beside the model picker (**Credits left**) shows how many are left. Click it to see them, with **Get more credits** and **See usage**.
- When a message needs more credits than are left, the message box says so and offers **Get more credits**.

Your own API key and an outside AI tool use no credits.

## Use your own API key

1. In Preferences, open **BYOAI**.
2. Under **Your own API key**, click **Add key** beside Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter, and paste the key.
3. Click **Check key**. JusPrin checks it with the provider and keeps it on this computer only. **Replace** and **Remove** change it later.

The provider bills you for what you use.

![Preferences, BYOAI, with the API key rows and the AI tools found on this computer](pictures/ai-chats-and-account/byoai.png)

## Connect an AI tool you already use

An AI app such as Claude Code or Codex can work on the project open in JusPrin.

1. In Preferences, open **BYOAI**. Under **Connect an AI tool you already use**, each tool says whether it was found on this computer. **Look again** searches again.
2. Click **Connect…** beside the tool. For some tools JusPrin shows a command to run, with **Copy**; for others it shows the change it will make to the tool's settings, and **Connect** makes it.
3. When it says **Connected**, click **Done**. The tool can now see and change the open project.

Names in bold are the words on screen. On a Mac the menus named here are in the menu bar. On Windows and Linux the **File** menu is the **File** button in the title bar, and the other menus are in the menu beside it.

## Open Preferences

- On a Mac, choose **Preferences** in the JusPrin menu, or press Cmd+,.
- On Windows and Linux, choose **Preferences** in the menu beside the **File** button, or press Ctrl+,.
- In a project, the "…" button at the right of the header has **Preferences…**. On Home, it is the gear button at the top right.

The window lists its sections at the left: **Account**, **BYOAI**, **Appearance**, **3D view**, **Projects & files** and **Updates**. Account and BYOAI set up AI; the guide's page on AI chats describes them. **More preferences…** at the bottom opens the app's full list of older preferences.

## Language, theme and units

In Preferences, open **Appearance**.

- **Language**: pick one from the list. JusPrin uses it after it restarts, and offers **Restart now** or **Later**. Restart now saves the project first.
- **Theme**: **Light** or **Dark**. The change shows at once.
- **Units**: **Millimetres** or **Inches**.

![Preferences, Appearance, with Language, Theme and Units](pictures/the-app/appearance.png)

## Mouse and touchpad in the 3D view

In Preferences, open **3D view**.

- **Controls**: **Mouse** or **Touchpad**, for how dragging and scrolling move the view.
- **Zoom toward the pointer** zooms to where the pointer is, instead of the middle of the view. **Reverse scroll-wheel zoom** turns the wheel's direction around. **Turn freely** lets the view turn past upside down.
- Under **Mouse buttons**, choose what **Left-drag**, **Middle-drag** and **Right-drag** do: **Turn the view**, **Pan** or **Nothing**.

The keys of the 3D view are listed under **Keyboard Shortcuts** in the **Help** menu.

![Preferences, 3D view, with the controls and what each mouse button does](pictures/the-app/3d-view.png)

## Show and hide the panels

An open project has a panel at the left, with the plates and the project, and the AI panel at the right.

- On a Mac, the **View** menu has **Show plates and project panel** and **Show AI panel**, which read **Hide…** while the panel is shown.
- On Windows and Linux, the **View** menu has **Plates and project panel** and **AI panel**, ticked while each is shown.
- The header has a button for each: at its far left for the plates panel, at its far right for the AI panel.
- **Home** in the **View** menu goes back to Home.

## Classic view

Classic view is the app's original screen, with all print settings in a panel at the side. Choose **Switch to classic view…** in the **View** menu, or in the "…" menu at the right of the header. To return, click **Back to JusPrin** on the bar across the top, or choose **Switch to JusPrin view** in the **View** menu.

## Updates

JusPrin looks for a newer version once a day, on GitHub. When there is one, **Updates** in Preferences is marked with a dot.

1. In Preferences, open **Updates**. **Check now** looks straight away.
2. When it says **JusPrin {v} is available** with the version, click **Download**. The release's page opens in your browser; download and install it from there.
3. **Skip this version** stops it asking about that version. **Release notes** shows what changed.

Untick **New JusPrin versions** to stop the daily check. The printer and filament profiles that come with JusPrin are updated with JusPrin itself.

![Preferences, Updates, with Check now and the choice of what to check for](pictures/the-app/updates.png)

## Report a problem or get help

- **Report a problem…** in the **Help** menu opens a new issue on JusPrin's GitHub page in your browser, with the app's version and your system already filled in. Nothing is sent until you submit it there.
- **JusPrin guide…** in the **Help** menu opens this guide inside the app, with a search box.
- **Ask AI…** in the **Help** menu opens the AI panel.
- **About JusPrin** shows the version, with **Copy version**, and how to get help. It is in the JusPrin menu on a Mac and in the **Help** menu on Windows and Linux.

## Quit

On a Mac, choose **Quit** in the JusPrin menu (Cmd+Q). On Windows choose **Exit** in the **File** menu, and on Linux **Quit** in the **File** menu.

   **Harness patterns** (tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp; mode docs at lines 6–~360)

   - Canvas GL readback (`glReadPixels`) gives the 3D view's own pixels.
   - Modal dialogs are handled with `answer_modals(id)` plus `m_modal_gate` (a lambda called every 200 ms; return false to keep the dialog open).

   - Waiting uses `wait_until(cond, name, then, each_tick)` and `wait_until_settled`.
   - `JUSPRIN_SOURCE_DIR` is defined for the harness.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Checks the app guide against the running app and takes its pictures.

guide_checks.json names, for each page of docs/guide, the shell harness runs
that walk the screens the page describes. Each run drives the real app in a
data folder of its own, asserts what it finds (HARNESS CHECK lines) and writes
pictures of it. This script runs them, fails when a run fails, and copies the
pictures a page uses into docs/guide/pictures/<page>/, so a page's steps and
its pictures are both taken from the app as built.

    tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py                  every page
    tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py --area print-settings
    tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py --list           what would run; runs nothing

The harness is the newest one under build/ (the shell_integration_harness
target), or JUSPRIN_SHELL_HARNESS. A run opens the app's window on this
computer's screen and takes real clicks: leave the screen unlocked and the
computer alone while it runs, about a minute a page. A run that fails is tried
once more before it counts. On a Mac grant Screen Recording to the program that starts this script (and to
the harness, if macOS asks), or the whole-window pictures come out black. A
black picture is refused, never copied. Pictures the app draws by itself, the
AI panel's and the plates panel's, need neither.
--keep DIR keeps every run's log and all the pictures it wrote. The pictures
step needs Pillow (pip install pillow).
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import pathlib
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
CHECKS = json.loads((HERE / "guide_checks.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
PICTURES = ROOT / "docs/guide/pictures"
HARNESS_NAMES = ("JusPrinShellHarness", "shell_integration_harness", "shell_integration_harness.exe")


def harness():
    named = os.environ.get("JUSPRIN_SHELL_HARNESS")
    if named:
        return pathlib.Path(named)
    built = [path for name in HARNESS_NAMES for path in (ROOT / "build").rglob(name) if path.is_file()]
    if not built:
        sys.exit("the shell harness is not built: build the shell_integration_harness target or set JUSPRIN_SHELL_HARNESS")
    return max(built, key=lambda path: path.stat().st_mtime)


def run(binary, entry, out, log):
    """One harness run. Returns whether the page's part of it passed, what
    failed in that part, how many checks passed, and what failed elsewhere.

    An entry with "checks" depends on those named checks alone: the run is
    stopped once they have passed, and a failure elsewhere in it is reported
    apart, since it is not about the page. Without "checks" the whole run
    has to pass. The harness gives up by itself after 900 s."""
    args = [str(out) if arg == "{dir}" else arg for arg in entry["args"]]
    env = dict(os.environ, **{name: str(out) if value == "{dir}" else value for name, value in entry.get("env", {}).items()})
    needed = set(entry.get("checks", []))
    if needed:
        # A run stopped early never removes its data folder, which the harness makes in the
        # temporary folder: put that beside the run, to remove it here. Only for these runs:
        # the printer menu's run takes ten minutes instead of six seconds with it moved.
        env["TMPDIR"] = str(out / "data")
        (out / "data").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    passed, failed, lines = set(), [], []
    process = subprocess.Popen([str(binary), *args], env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                               text=True, errors="replace")
    for line in process.stdout:
        lines.append(line)
        check = re.search(r"HARNESS CHECK (\S+) (PASS|FAIL)", line)
        if check:
            (passed.add if check.group(2) == "PASS" else failed.append)(check.group(1))
        if needed and (needed <= passed or needed & set(failed)):
            process.terminate()

## Slice and print

The button at the right of the header of the project does the next step for the plate you are working on:

- **Slice** while the plate is not sliced. Cmd+R on a Mac, Ctrl+R on Windows and Linux, does the same.
- **Slicing…** while it slices. The button beside it turns into an X, **Cancel slicing**, that stops it.
- **Print** once the plate is sliced, or "Print plate 2" and so on when the project has more plates. It opens the window that sends the print to the printer, where you start it. Switching to a plate that is not sliced brings **Slice** back.

The arrow beside the button (**Print actions**) has the other choices: **Slice all plates**, and once a plate is sliced, **Check Print**, **Print all plates…** and **Export sliced file…**. The **Print** menu has the same commands.

![The header of a sliced project, with Print plate 2 and the arrow beside it](pictures/slicing-and-printing/print-button.png)

When the printer has no connection set up, Print says **Printer connection required**: connect the printer first (the guide's page on printers describes it), or save the sliced file and print from a memory card.

## Check the print before printing
## Print history

JusPrin keeps a record of every sliced file it sent or saved, with a copy of the file.

- On Home, click **Print history** above the projects, or the history line on a project's or a printer's card.
- In a project, click **Print history** in the Project tab of the panel at the left.

![Print history, with an exported file and the Print again and Export… buttons](pictures/slicing-and-printing/print-history.png)

Each entry says where the file went and when, and whether the print finished. **Print again** sends the kept copy to the printer again, **Export…** saves it again, and **Open in chat** goes to the chat the print was made in. Type in **Search prints** to find one.

When you are signed in to a JusPrin account, an entry in Print history offers "Share how it printed and get 25 credits". It opens **Tell us how it printed**: add a photo with **Choose a photo…**, write what happened in at least 200 characters, say whether **It worked**, came out **Partly** or not, and click **Send report**. Each sliced file takes one report.

## Calibrate a printer or a filament

"""Checks the app guide (docs/guide) from end to end, and rebuilds what is

import sys

def main():

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Does the project chat's model answer a how-to question from the app guide?

Each question in guide_questions.json belongs to one page of docs/guide. A run
sends the question as a chat's first message and passes when the model's reply
tells the person what the question's "answer" says, in the judge's reading. The
run's line also says whether the model read the page's skill
(skills/guide-<area>/SKILL.md) on the way.

The request is the recorded "advice-infill" point with the person's sentence
replaced, so the prompt, the tools and the workspace are the app's, and a
skill_read of a guide is answered with the skill as checked in. Everything
else is run_prompt_tests.py: the same options, backends and judge.

    tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --runs 1
    tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py --area print-settings --no-guide ...

--area keeps the questions of one page. --no-guide takes every guide off the
list skill_read carries, which is the app before the guide: the gap between
the two runs is what the guide does.
"""
import copy
import json
import pathlib
import sys

import run_prompt_tests as runner

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SKILLS = HERE / "../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills"
QUESTIONS = json.loads((HERE / "guide_questions.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
POINT = "advice-infill"


def skill_text(area):
    """The text skill_read returns: the skill file after its front matter."""
    return (SKILLS / f"guide-{area}" / "SKILL.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8").split("\n---\n", 1)[1].strip()


def add_case(area, entry, with_guide):
    skill = f"guide-{area}"

    class GuideQuestion(runner.Case):
        def check(self, step):
            if step.tool:
                return (runner.FAIL if step.changes() else runner.CONTINUE), str(step)
            read = any("skill_read" in line and skill in line for line in self.log)
            yes, why = self.judged(step, f"Does the assistant's last message tell the person {entry['answer']}?")
            tag = "[read the guide] " if read else "[did not read the guide] "
            return (runner.PASS, tag + str(step)) if yes else (runner.FAIL, tag + "WRONG OR MISSING PLACE: " + why)

    GuideQuestion.name = f"guide-{area}-{entry['id']}"
    GuideQuestion.__doc__ = entry["question"]
    point = copy.deepcopy(runner.REQUESTS[POINT])
    point["body"]["input"][0]["content"][0]["text"] = entry["question"]
    if with_guide:
        answer = copy.deepcopy(next(a for a in point["answers"] if a["tool"] == "skill_read"))
        output = json.loads(answer["output"])
        output["result"] = {"name": skill, "text": skill_text(area)}
        answer["arguments"] = {"name": skill}
        answer["output"] = json.dumps(output, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
        point["answers"].append(answer)
    runner.REQUESTS[GuideQuestion.name] = point
    runner.CASES[GuideQuestion.name] = GuideQuestion
    return GuideQuestion.name


def take(flag, has_value):
    """Removes this script's own option from the command line and returns it."""
    if flag not in sys.argv:
        return None
    at = sys.argv.index(flag)
    value = sys.argv[at + 1] if has_value else True
    del sys.argv[at:at + (2 if has_value else 1)]
    return value


def main():
    area = take("--area", True)
    with_guide = not take("--no-guide", False)
    if area is not None and area not in QUESTIONS:
        sys.exit(f"no questions for {area}: guide_questions.json has {', '.join(sorted(QUESTIONS))}")
    if not with_guide:
        tool = next(tool for tool in runner.TOOLS if tool.get("name") == "skill_read")
        tool["description"] = "\n".join(line for line in tool["description"].split("\n") if not line.startswith("- guide-"))
    names = [add_case(each, entry, with_guide)
             for each in sorted(QUESTIONS) if area in (None, each) for entry in QUESTIONS[each]]
    if "--case" not in sys.argv:
        for name in names:
            sys.argv += ["--case", name]
    # The runner's default spreads its whole budget over the cases named.
    if "--runs" not in sys.argv:

I committed the six missing guide pages as b49541e109 on `claude/guide-pages`, not pushed. `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` passes. On Sonnet through the Claude subscription, all 37 questions were answered right in all 3 runs each, 111 of 111.

**What was written**
- Six pages, listed in this order in `docs/guide/README.md` and in Help › JusPrin guide…:
  - Projects and files
  - Plates and objects
  - Printers and filament
  - Print settings (the existing page)
  - Slicing, checking and printing
  - AI chats, account and credits
  - The app itself
- The division follows your proposed split; the code gave no reason to change it.
- Each page is written from the code, and every bold label is found in the source by the test.
- Every section has a harness run with named checks.
- There are 28 new questions in `guide_questions.json`.

**Harness changes**
- A new run opens Preferences, clicks through each section, and checks that the Help guide window lists all seven pages in order.
- Keys pressed on the 3D view now send key-down as well as the character. Since the OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 merge the 3D view only opens its tools on key-down, so the existing R-key check had been failing. The C, L, P, H and F keys the plates page names are now checked the same way.
- New checks cover File › New project, Open recent, Export project 3MF and the Import submenu.

**Per page, right answers and whether its own page was read**
- Plates and objects, printers and filament, slicing and printing, AI chats, and the app itself: all 15 of 15 each, and the page was always read.
- Projects and files: 15 of 15. For "add a second STL" the model read the plates page instead, and answered right.
- Print settings: 24 of 24. For "get back from classic view" it read the app page instead, and answered right.

The test runner used to answer only a read of the question's own page, so I changed it to answer a read of any guide page and say which one was read.

Two fixes to make the measurement fair:
- The page descriptions are now about 200 bytes and have no "…". The Claude command-line tool cuts a tool description past about 2,000 characters, so the last pages' descriptions would have been dropped. It also rewrites "…" as "...". The guide README now says so.
- Three questions were reworded. The test project has no warnings, so "there's a warning, make it go away" made the model rightly say it saw none.

**Tests passed**
- The full AgentUI suite (762 tests) and the type check.
- `agent_bridge_tests '[project]'`, after regenerating `project_tools.json`.
- The prompt suite's unit tests.
- clang-tidy on my lines. Its other 12 findings are in files changed by earlier commits.

**Pictures missing and why**
- There is no version-history picture. The run that restores a version draws the panel as a 20×20 blank square, and the run that does draw it has no saved versions yet.
- Pictures of the 3D view are read straight from the view, because whole-window screen grabs come out black here.

**Still open**
- The live prompt suite has to run before merge. I did not run it.
- The Help window packs every picture into the AI panel's page, which grew from 1.3 MB to 4.3 MB.
- Problems that were already there:
